item.title: Iran missile hits US-linked ship near Hormuz, many injured? Trump's losses grow amid Houthi fear?
item.description: Tensions around the Middle East’s key waterways have intensified, with reports alleging that Iran targeted a U.S.-contracted vessel near the Strait of Hormuz using drones and a missile. At least one projectile reportedly struck the ship, causing minor injuries, including smoke inhalation, while several U.S. personnel were said to be aboard. The reports emerged as Washington was reportedly holding talks with Houthi representatives in Oman over security guarantees for American shipping. Separately, the Houthis claimed they shot down a Saudi F-15 fighter jet over Yemen, though the claim has not been independently verified. The developments add to growing maritime tensions across the region.

item.title: Putin's missile response to US' new bill targeting Russian oil buyers? Kyiv set on fire at midnight
item.description: Russia launched a major missile and drone attack on Kyiv overnight on 16–17 September 2026, with over 10 blasts rocking the capital as ballistic missiles struck residential and education facilities, injuring at least 12 people. The strike came as the U.S. House passed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, targeting Moscow's energy revenues and buyers with up to 100% tariffs. Sent to President Trump for signature, the bill marks fresh U.S. pressure on Putin's war machine. Is this escalation a warning—or the start of a deeper confrontation?

With the new Mecca defence pact facing its first major test, Riyadh is looking to strengthen its air defences as pressure from the Houthis continues to mount.
